comment: I've heard that Pollock is great for lecture, but she seems totally different in lab. She gets quickly agitated if you're not 100% certain of everything you're doing and the rationale behind it. Outside of a lab setting, she's seems great though.

Dr. Pollock is a very solid biochem professor. While she does expect her students to understand a large swath of material, she is exceptionally fair with her exam questions and provides plenty of practice material ahead of time. Extremely organized and clear, and she is funny enough to make lectures entertaining. Put in the time, and you'll be ok.

The reason I am no longer pre-med; do not take if you have the option. Willing to meet with you outside of class but come prepared with thoughtful questions because she can be demeaning and will literally just stare at you. Not good at explaining and then questions why students don't understand.

Dr Pollock is super knowledgable about biochemistry but can come across as slightly intimidating if you are unsure of what you are doing. Make sure to do lots of prep-work before you go into class/ lab. If you put in the work you can get an A. One of the smartest professors you will ever have.

Do not take Pollock for biochemistry lab. She is SO passive aggressive and makes you feel stupid for asking any sort of question. Her procedures and grading isn't clear AT ALL and then she proceeds to get mad at students for being confused. She is a very picky grader as well. I would not recommend.

Organic Chemistry is challenging, no matter who you take it with, but Dr. Pollock makes it manageable. A lot of time outside of class needs to be taken to learn as her lectures are fast-paced; however, if you do the work, you should be fine. Be sure to ask questions, especially on homework and test wrappers (where you gain back points on tests).

Very amazing at explaining concepts. That being said, please please please live breathe and eat organic chemistry to pass this class. If you think you understand a topic, go back at it again. The little details matter so much in organic chemistry so definitely ask questions if you EVER feel confused. Do not assume anything is common sense.

Dr. Pollock genuinely cares about her students and is more than willing to help them outside of class. However, I did find it hard to ask questions during class time as she moved so fast through the material.

I absolutely loved Professor Pollock! She is an amazing lecturer & is always open to reexplain concepts to students in other ways. There is only one hw assignment per week & her practice exams are almost identical to the actual. She is picky when grading but this ensures students learn material & she gives exam corrections!

Dr. Pollock cares deeply about her students and wants them to succeed, but also likes to challenge them. Tests are difficult especially compared to other professors in the department, but she offers test corrections to accommodate and is always willing to help. She provokes students to think deeply about organic chemistry. Take her if you can!!
easily one of the top 5 profs at UR. so nice and super helpful. take her class if you can!!

Dr. Pollock was insanely organized, which is an important quality when it comes to organic. Her organization helped me succeed in the class and made learning orgo a whole lot enjoyable. You will need to put in many hours reserved for practice and review in order to do well in the class. She provides numerous practice problems for each unit as well.

Pollock goes through material really quickly and sometimes forgets to slow down for students. Homework was graded on accuracy which was difficult sometimes. Tests were not terrible but unlike some other orgo teachers, you have to memorize all the mechanisms and can't use a cheat sheet. She does give extra credit and is available outside of class.

Fav professor this sem! She expects a lot from students at this level, as she should, and makes that very clear. Sometimes this will get to you, so you just have to remember it's only to make you a better student. If you can keep that in mind, you'll see she's an AMAZING professor and a great person who cares so much about her students.

Dr. Pollock is a solid professor. She is extremely kind and willing to help students who reach out to her. However, lectures throughout the semester were extremely rushed, leaving the majority of learning to myself outside the classroom, on top of studying for exams and other classes. Exams including the final make up over 70% of your grade.

Professor uses the excuse of having a child to not be available for office hours. Even though, she is the one who sets up her office hours or makes them during impossible times. She creates a class environment where one feels helpless and afraid to ask for help. She expects students to learn over 20+ reactions in a span of two weeks. DO NO TAKE.

Dr. Pollock is truly understanding, considerate, and caring. Despite the reputation of orgo, she was super willing to provide her students with any resources, including recording clarification videos. There's a lot of material in the course, meaning most classes are pretty much lectures which can get boring at times. Good amount of extra credit too

Dr. Pollock is my favorite professor at UR. Orgo is definitely killer but it is going to be with any professor. She is super fair with grading and gives you everything you will need to succeed (practice problems, practice exams, review sessions, etc.). if you take someone else you are making a mistake.

Not good at explaining key concepts. I had to teach myself everything. Dr. Pollock doesn't understand how to explain concepts. I was not the only student with this problem. She is a picky grader. Not worth taking her class. I will be avoiding taking any other classes with her. Students warned me not to take her and I should've listened.

Awful professor. A very picky grader. Tries to take away points instead of giving them. Does not explain concepts well. Take a different professor for Organic Chemistry. I have not met a single person in my class who actually thinks she is a decent teacher.

Biochem is a hard subject and Dr. Pollock tries her best to make it understandable, which works but in the end it's up to you to put in the hours 326 needs to pass. Her exams are tough and she's a picky grader.  Put in work and you'll do well.

Dr. Pollock is my favorite chem professor I've had so far. She lectures very well and includes models and extra practice problems. As long as you work hard, you will do well. She is also very helpful outside of class for extra questions. She really cares about her students and I highly recommend her.
